question: What is the primary function of the gallbladder?
explanation: The gallbladder acts as a reservoir that holds bile made by the liver until it is needed for fat digestion. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h1)

question: How do gallstones usually start forming inside the biliary system?

options.A: Chemical imbalances causing solid particles to form in the bile
options.B: Calcium deposits traveling up from the small intestine
options.C: Excess protein buildup in the liver ducts

explanation: You've got this! Stones start forming when components in bile, like cholesterol and bilirubin, become imbalanced and clump together. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h1)

question: Choledocholithiasis means there are gallstones in which part of the body?
explanation: Nice work! Choledocholithiasis happens when stones slip out of the gallbladder and get trapped right inside the common bile duct. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which patient has the highest risk of developing cholesterol gallstones?

options.A: An elderly male who exercises daily and eats low-fat meals
options.B: An adolescent male eating a high-protein diet
options.C: A young adult female with a low body mass index
options.D: A middle-aged female who lost weight very rapidly

explanation: Great thinking! Being female, middle-aged, and undergoing rapid weight loss are classic risk factors due to hormonal shifts and bile changes. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is Murphy's sign used to check for during a physical exam?
explanation: Spot on! Murphy's sign is a classic way doctors and nurses check for gallbladder inflammation by pressing gently on the right upper belly while the patient takes a deep breath. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why do some patients with gallbladder disease develop jaundice (yellow skin)?

options.A: Bilirubin backs up into the bloodstream because a bile duct is blocked
options.B: Fatty foods destroy the skin's surface pigments
options.C: The liver stops producing red blood cells
options.D: Stomach acid leaks through the gallbladder wall

explanation: You nailed it! When a stone blocks the bile duct, bilirubin cannot flow to the intestines, so it builds up in the blood and turns the skin yellow. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is usually the very first imaging test done to check for gallstones?
explanation: Spot on! Ultrasound is fast, safe, painless, and very good at spotting gallstones and inflamed gallbladder walls. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which lab result strongly suggests that a bile duct is blocked?

options.C: Elevated serum bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase

explanation: Great job! When bile cannot flow out, these specific liver enzymes and bilirubin spill over into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the medical term for the surgical removal of the gallbladder?
explanation: You got it! A cholecystectomy is simply the surgical removal of the gallbladder, done either through tiny camera cuts or an open incision. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why are patients with gallbladder issues advised to eat a low-fat diet?

options.A: Fat stops the liver from making any bile
options.B: Low-fat foods mean you don't need digestive enzymes
options.C: Fat intake makes the gallbladder squeeze, which causes pain

explanation: Spot on! Fats trigger hormones that tell the gallbladder to squeeze. If stones are blocking the way, that squeezing causes sharp pain. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why do many patients feel shoulder pain shortly after laparoscopic gallbladder surgery?

options.A: Trapped carbon dioxide gas irritating the phrenic nerve
options.B: Muscle strain from lifting heavy things too early
options.C: Infection in the shoulder joint from bad positioning
options.D: Direct nerve damage from surgical tools

explanation: You've got this! The gas used to inflate the belly during surgery can irritate the diaphragm, causing a weird referred pain up in the shoulder. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of these after-surgery symptoms should a patient report right away?

options.A: Mild tiredness during the first week at home
options.B: Severe, worsening belly pain with a high fever
options.C: Minor bruising around the tiny incision sites

explanation: Spot on! Severe pain and high fever are red flags that could mean an infection, a leak, or other serious complications. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h6)
